newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-SWISS ZUELLE JOINS FESTINA IN HUGE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-SWISS ZUELLE JOINS FESTINA IN HUGE DEAL.

text.p: World time trial champion Alex Zuelle on Wednesday signed a contract from 1998 with the Festina team worth an estimated 10 million Swiss francs ($6.7 million) over three years.

The Swiss rider, who pulled out of the Tour de France in the first week after being involved in a string of falls, signed for two years with an option for a third during the French classic's brief passage through Switzerland.

Zuelle, who won the 1996 Vuelta, ended his Tour prematurely because he did not want to take more risks after breaking his collarbone during the Tour of Switzerland two weeks before the start of the French race.
The 28-year-old Swiss rider recently said: "I'm very happy at Once (team), but the offer is too big to say no."
Zuelle joins compatriot Laurent Dufaux and Richard Virenque of France in the Spanish-based team.
Festina team manager Bruno Roussel hinted that Zuelle could lead the team in the Giro d'Italia, but said Virenque would remain Festina's leader in the Tour de France.
